genZNote: Urease turns urine alkaline, alkaline urine grows staghorn stones — one biochemical reaction, one entire urology consult.

morphology.motility: Highly motile with peritrichous flagella; produces characteristic swarming growth

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, water, and the intestinal tract of humans and animals
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora; opportunistic pathogen, especially of the urinary tract

culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe; characteristic swarming motility produces concentric rings on non-selective agar
culture.colonyMorphology: Swarming, wave-like colonies on blood agar; colorless (non-lactose fermenting) colonies on MacConkey agar

identificationClues: Swarming motility on blood agar (concentric ring pattern)
Indole negative — distinguishes from P. vulgaris

virulenceFactors: Urease (splits urea to ammonia, alkalinizes urine, promotes struvite stone formation)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous from GI flora; catheter-associated nosocomial transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Common cause of complicated and catheter-associated UTIs; strongly associated with struvite (infection) kidney stones
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Swarming motility on non-selective media is a classic identifying feature but can overgrow other organisms on a mixed culture plate

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Urease positive, indole negative, H2S positive
examFacts.importantTest: Swarming motility on blood agar; urease test
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Urease production alkalinizes urine, predisposing to struvite (staghorn) calculi
